source.question: Was F-12's falling oil rate in 2011-2013 a loss of reservoir pressure or water taking over the well? How much oil was left before an uneconomic water cut?

findings.claim: F-12's oil rate fell from 1 444 to 268 Sm3/d in 2011-2013, while liquid held near 5 096 Sm3/d with the choke fully open.
findings.detail: Oil rate per producing day from monthly data; liquid and choke from yearly waterflood diagnostics showing capacity take-over.

findings.claim: The fall was water taking capacity: water cut rose from 72% to 95% and WOR rose to 18.
findings.detail: Water cut and WOR from monthly diagnostics; gauge failure means pressure cannot be checked directly.

findings.claim: Reservoir pressure was supported: voidage replacement was 1.02 in 2013 and the field reached its 0.80 design water cut without exceeding liquid capacity.
findings.detail: Field voidage ratio near one; design limit from plan; field liquid capacity versus design.

findings.claim: F-12 had already passed 80% water cut in February 2012, about 48 months after first oil.
findings.detail: Threshold crossing for water cut above 0.80 recorded in events.

findings.claim: About 189 140 Sm3 of oil was left before a 95% water cut on the WOR trend, with the 80% and 90% limits already passed.
findings.detail: WOR trend fitted on recent months with high water cut; extrapolation to economic limit.

submission.summary: F-12's 2011-2013 oil fall was water taking over, not pressure loss: liquid stayed near 5 096 Sm3/d with the choke at 100% while water cut rose from 72% to 95%. Field voidage stayed near 1.02 and about 189 140 Sm3 remained before a 95% water cut.

issues.text: downhole pressure gauge reads 0 (1106 days, 826,952 Sm3 oil produced without pressure data)
oil rate per producing day down 47% over the last 90 days (520 -> 275 Sm3/d)
water cut above 0.80 (now 0.84); the platform was designed for 0.80

result.levels: alarm: act now; caution: watch; note: for the record

result.summary: 30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.05 on 2009-10-31, 21 months after first oil.
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.5 on 2010-06-04, 28 months after first oil.
Shut in for 12 days from 2010-08-16. Oil rate 1,821 -> 2,000 Sm3/d (+10%) after restart. Same time as F-14.

bhp_bar reads 0 on 1106 days from 2010-10-12 to 2013-12-31 while the well kept flowing on 966 days (826,952 Sm3 oil): a sensor failure, not a pressure collapse. Last good reading: 253.9 on 2010-10-11.
Shut in for 10 days from 2011-06-21. Oil rate 1,144 -> 1,364 Sm3/d (+19%) after restart. Same time as F-14.
Shut in for 20 days from 2011-10-16. Oil rate 955 -> 1,158 Sm3/d (+21%) after restart. Same time as F-14.
Shut in for 11 days from 2012-01-03. Oil rate 1,063 -> 1,028 Sm3/d (-3%) after restart. Same time as F-14.
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.8 on 2012-02-14, 48 months after first oil.
Shut in for 46 days from 2012-08-14. Oil rate 691 -> 728 Sm3/d (+5%) after restart. Same time as F-14.
Shut in for 13 days from 2013-03-12. Oil rate 531 -> 572 Sm3/d (+8%) after restart.

result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

volve_pud.title: Plan for utbygging og drift av Volve (PUD, plan for development and operation)

rows: The field maximum water cut is 0,80.
The compressor can also be used for gas lift of the production wells on Volve, which may be necessary for wells with high water cut.
Kompressoren kan også benyttes til å gassløfte produksjonsbrønnene på Volve, noe som kan bli nødvendig for brønner med høyt vannkutt.
Produced water volumes are expected to be relatively limited and the water will be injected together with Utsira water as pressure support in the reservoir.
Produserte vannvolumer forventes å være relativt begrenset. Vannet vil bli injisert sammen med Utsiravann som trykkstøtte i reservoaret.

Continuous discharges of drilling mud and cuttings to sea will occur only from drilling of the wells' upper sections where water-based mud is used, the mud will be attempted reused, and there will be no discharge to sea of oil-based mud or cuttings.

Kontinuerlige utslipp av boreslam og borekaks til sjø vil kun skje fra boring av brønnenes øverste seksjoner hvor det nyttes vannbasert slam. Boreslammet vil bli forsøkt gjenbrukt. Det vil ikke være utslipp til sjø av oljebasert slam eller kaks.

Table 9.3 shows planned discharge of water-based drilling fluid and cuttings drilled with water-based drilling fluid is 5673 m3 drilling fluid and 1137 m3 cuttings for 3 production wells, 4485 m3 drilling fluid and 2115 m3 cuttings for 3 injection wells, and 2304 m3 drilling fluid and 710 m3 cuttings for 2 water producers.
Well F-11 B has a water depth / airgap of 91.0 m MSL / 54.9 m RT
Water depth / airgap: 91,0 m MSL / 54.9 m RT
Well F-11 B WH, Riser and BOP were washed reciprocating the washing assembly across the specified areas with 1500 lpm and the Riser was displaced by sea water.
Washed WH, Riser and BOP reciprocating the washing assy. across the specified areas, w/ 1500 lpm. Riser was displaced by sea water.
The riser and BOP were displaced to seawater with 2200 lpm and 10 bar.
Displaced riser and BOP to seawater with 2200 lpm and 10 bar.

result.scope: whole field, all producers and injectors summed per day, then per month
result.plan_source: Plan for utbygging og drift av Volve (PUD, plan for development and operation), page 23, Table 4.3

water_sm3_per_day.limit: field water handling (derived: liquid capacity x maximum water cut)

result.plan_end_quote: Kumulativ oljeproduksjon inntil minimum økonomisk rate på 2.100 Sm3 /d (gitt Volve oljepris på 18,7 USD/fat) nås er 11,4 MSm3
result.note: These are field and platform limits (PUD p.35 lists the same platform capacities); compare them with field totals, never one well. The maximum water cut is a share at full liquid rate: the water the platform can handle is liquid capacity x maximum water cut (water_sm3_per_day). The field reaching that share at a lower liquid rate means it ran at the design water cut, not over its water capacity. Rates are per calendar day of each month.

arguments.sql: SELECT date, bhp_bar, whp_bar, choke_pct, oil_sm3, water_sm3, on_stream_hrs FROM production_daily WHERE well='F-12' AND date BETWEEN '2011-01-01' AND '2013-12-31' AND on_stream_hrs >= 12 ORDER BY date LIMIT 5
